an3.40:1.3: Oneself as one’s authority, the world as one’s authority, and the Dhamma as one’s authority.
an3.40:1.4: (1) “And what, bhikkhus, is oneself as one’s authority?
an3.40:1.5: Here, having gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut, a bhikkhu reflects thus:
an3.40:1.6: ‘I did not go forth from the household life into homelessness for the sake of a robe,
an3.40:1.7: almsfood, or lodging, or for the sake of becoming this or that,
an3.40:1.8: but rather with the thought: “I am immersed in birth, old age, and death; in sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and anguish. I am immersed in suffering, afflicted by suffering.
an3.40:1.9: Perhaps an ending of this entire mass of suffering can be discerned.”
an3.40:1.10: As one who has gone forth from the household life into homelessness, it would not be proper for me to seek out sensual pleasures similar to or worse than those that I have discarded.’
an3.40:1.12: ‘Energy will be aroused in me without slackening; mindfulness will be established without confusion; my body will be tranquil without disturbance; my mind will be concentrated and one-pointed.’
an3.40:1.13: Having taken himself as his authority, he abandons the unwholesome and develops the wholesome; he abandons what is blameworthy and develops what is blameless; he maintains himself in purity.
an3.40:1.14: This is called oneself as one’s authority.
an3.40:2.1: (2) “And what, bhikkhus, is the world as one’s authority?
an3.40:2.2: Here, having gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut, a bhikkhu reflects thus:
an3.40:2.3: ‘I did not go forth from the household life into homelessness for the sake of a robe …
an3.40:2.5: but rather with the thought: “I am immersed in birth, old age, and death …
an3.40:2.6: Perhaps an ending of this entire mass of suffering can be discerned.”
an3.40:2.7: As one who has gone forth from the household life into homelessness, I might think sensual thoughts, thoughts of ill will, or thoughts of harming. But the abode of the world is vast.
an3.40:2.8: In the vast abode of the world there are ascetics and brahmins with psychic potency and the divine eye who know the minds of others.
an3.40:2.9: They see things from a distance but they are not themselves seen even when they’re close; they know the minds of others with their own mind.
an3.40:2.11: “Look at this clansman: though he has gone forth from the household life into homelessness out of faith, he is tarnished by bad unwholesome states.”
an3.40:2.12: There are deities, too, with psychic potency and the divine eye who know the minds of others.
an3.40:2.13: They see even from a distance but are not seen themselves even when close; they too know the minds of others with their own mind.
an3.40:2.14: They too would know me thus:
an3.40:2.15: “Look at this clansman: though he has gone forth from the household life into homelessness out of faith, he is tarnished by bad unwholesome states.”’
an3.40:2.17: ‘Energy will be aroused in me without slackening; mindfulness will be established without confusion; my body will be tranquil without disturbance; my mind will be concentrated and one-pointed.’
an3.40:2.18: Having taken the world as his authority, he abandons the unwholesome and develops the wholesome; he abandons what is blameworthy and develops what is blameless; he maintains himself in purity.
an3.40:2.19: This is called the world as one’s authority.
an3.40:3.1: (3) “And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma as one’s authority?
an3.40:3.2: Here, having gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut, a bhikkhu reflects thus:
an3.40:3.3: ‘I did not go forth from the household life into homelessness for the sake of a robe …
an3.40:3.5: but rather with the thought: “I am immersed in birth, old age, and death …
an3.40:3.6: Perhaps an ending of this entire mass of suffering can be discerned.”
an3.40:3.7: The Dhamma is well expounded by the Blessed One, directly visible, immediate, inviting one to come and see, applicable, to be personally experienced by the wise.
an3.40:3.8: There are fellow monks of mine who know and see.
an3.40:3.9: As one who has gone forth from the household life into homelessness in this well-expounded Dhamma and discipline, it would be improper for me to be lazy and heedless.’
an3.40:3.11: ‘Energy will be aroused in me without slackening; mindfulness will be established without confusion; my body will be tranquil without disturbance; my mind will be concentrated and one-pointed.’
an3.40:3.12: Having taken the Dhamma as his authority, he abandons the unwholesome and develops the wholesome; he abandons what is blameworthy and develops what is blameless; he maintains himself in purity.
an3.40:3.13: This is called the Dhamma as one’s authority.
an3.40:4.1: For one performing an evil deed
an3.40:4.2: there is no place in the world called “hidden.”
an3.40:4.3: The self within you knows, O person,
an3.40:4.4: whether it is true or false.
an3.40:6.1: The devas and Tathāgatas see the fool
an3.40:6.3:
Therefore one should fare mindfully,
taking oneself as authority;
an3.40:6.4: alert and meditative, taking the world as authority;
an3.40:6.5:
and fare in accordance with the Dhamma,
taking the Dhamma as authority.
an3.40:6.6: Truly exerting himself, a sage does not decline.
an3.40:7.1:
Having vanquished Māra
and overcome the end-maker,
an3.40:7.2: the striver has finished with birth.
an3.40:7.3: Such a sage, wise, a world-knower,
